sample_unit: AAV patients in training (n=203) and validation (n=84) sets
models_evaluated: AI search tool combining text-mining with NLP-based exclusion

links.outcome: Sensitivity and PPV at training center versus external non-academic validation center
links.effect: Validation center: text-mining sensitivity 97.6%, PPV 58.2%; after NLP exclusion PPV 86.1%, sensitivity 98.0%. Training center: PPV 77.9%, sensitivity 96.3%. Performance held at the new site.
links.quote: In the validation center, text-mining identified 333 patients (sensitivity 97.6 % (95%CI [91.6, 99.7]), PPV 58.2 % (95%CI [52.8, 63.6])) and NLP-based exclusion resulted in 223 patients, increasing PPV to 86.1 % (95%CI [80.9, 90.4]) with 98.0 % (95%CI [94.9, 99.4]) sensitivity.

links.outcome: Patient identification performance compared with ICD-10 coding
links.effect: The AI identification method outperformed ICD-10 coding, mainly for MPO+ and organ-limited AAV patients.
links.quote: Our identification method outperformed ICD-10-coding predominantly in identifying MPO+ and organ-limited AAV patients.

unlisted_practices: Adding NLP-based exclusion to text-mining to improve positive predictive value of cohort identification

screen.reason: The paper focuses on model development and retrospective validation of an NLP/text-mining phenotyping algorithm to identify rare disease cohorts from EHRs for research purposes, without evaluating a clinical deployment, workflow, or organizational safeguard practice.
